subject: Processing loci, subprocessors, and deletion handback — GeoTech Labs Q&A
messages:
From: Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@geotechlabs.com>

Cc: security@geotechlabs.com
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Quick Q — where do model requests run & how does deletion handoff work?

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the demo earlier. Two quick questions from our security team as we prepare a short evidence packet for procurement:

1) For EU customers, can you confirm the exact locations where inference requests are executed (region/availability zone level if possible)? We need to state whether any processing ever leaves the EU.

2) Who are the subprocessors involved in network transit and model serving for the EU deployment (e.g., cloud partner, CDN, monitoring/storage vendors)? We need a current roster with country of operation.

3) Deletion: if we issue a customer-initiated data deletion (API call + support ticket), what are the chronological steps and estimated completion window for cached KV/prefix caches, ephemeral logs, and any backups? Who owns each step (Redwood vs subprocessor)?

If you have a short topology diagram and a CSV of subprocessors that we can attach to our procurement questionnaire, that would be ideal.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement is aiming to close next week.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Moreno
Head of IT Security | GeoTech Labs
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@geotechlabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2027 12:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick Q — where do model requests run & how does deletion handoff work?

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by attachments and next steps.

1) Execution loci (short): For EU customers who select EU-only processing, all inference execution and ephemeral storage occur in our EU regions (Frankfurt/eu-central-1 and Amsterdam/eu-west-1). We do not route inference traffic to non-EU regions when the EU-only option is enabled.

2) Subprocessors (short): Primary compute: RedCloud (managed GPU hosts, DE/IE); Edge CDN: CloudEdge EU POPs (MX/EU); Monitoring/log aggregation: LogHarbor (EU region); Backup snapshot custodians: StorageWorks (encrypted, EU). Full roster attached as CSV (redwood-subprocessors-20270904.csv) with country of operation and contract role.

3) Deletion handoff (short):
- Customer calls API to request deletion or opens a support ticket (timestamped).
- Redwood runtime evicts KV/prefix caches immediately for active model sessions (seconds-minutes).
- Ephemeral logs retained <72 hours by default in EU-only mode; permanent logs used for billing/metrics are truncated and anonymized per retention SLA — see SOC excerpt.
- Backup snapshots: retained per configured backup window — deletions are queued and applied on next snapshot cycle; we provide an ETA in the ticket.
- Responsibility: Redwood triggers eviction/erase for runtime caches and coordinates deletion requests with subprocessors. Subprocessors are contractually bound to apply deletion actions within stated windows; ownership is listed in the CSV.

I've attached: processing-topology-eu-only.pdf (topology diagram), redwood-subprocessors-20270904.csv (roster + country + role), and a SOC excerpt that references deletion/retention practices.

If your procurement team wants a one-page timeline tailored to your backup schedule, we can produce that — Marissa will help with the SLA language. Karthik has also offered to provide a short technical appendix for the packet describing how we ensure keys never leave EU KMS and how cross-border egress is prevented.

Would you like the timeline doc by EOD Monday?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Hi Alicia — quick technical appendix below that you can include in your packet. Happy to jump on a 20-minute call if you want to walk through any of the controls.

Technical appendix (copy-paste friendly):

Redwood Inference — EU-only processing controls (technical appendix)
1) KMS and key-wrap: For EU-only accounts we provision customer keys in our EU KMS tenant (Frankfurt). Keys never leave the EU: all key material is stored and used within EU-controlled hardware security modules (HSMs). When interacting with subprocessors (e.g., storage snapshots), we use key-wrap (AES-KW) within the EU boundary so wrapped objects remain unreadable outside the EU. Access to the KMS tenant is restricted via role-based access controls; admin access requires MFA + just-in-time access and is auditable.

2) KV/prefix cache eviction: The runtime maintains per-customer session state and a persistent KV cache sharded by region. For EU-only accounts, eviction calls are executed by the EU runtime manager which issues immediate cache delete operations across all live workers; there is also a background purge job to remove any stale entries. Cache eviction is synchronous from an API perspective — API returns success once in-memory and on-disk runtime caches acknowledge the delete.

3) Egress prevention & proof points: Network egress for EU-only accounts is restricted via VPC routing tables and policy enforcement at the service mesh layer. We configure strict allow-lists for outbound destinations; cross-region routes are disabled. Evidence we can supply: network ACL snapshots, routing table export, and a short packet showing recent test runs (we ran a zero-evidence egress test last quarter).

Backup deletion bound (conservative): In worst-case scenarios where a backup snapshot is scheduled and vendor apply cycles align, we commit to a conservative upper bound of 21 days for full deletion of backup copies in EU-only mode. Typical observed completion is <7 days. Subprocessor contracts require deletion within the committed window and Redwood escalates via contractual SLAs if a vendor exceeds that bound.

Ownership matrix (summary):
- Runtime caches / in-memory eviction: Redwood (immediate)
- Logs / aggregated telemetry: Redwood (truncate/anonymize) + subprocessor (if stored) — subprocessor applies deletion on vendor cycle (see CSV for vendor SLA)
- Backups / snapshots: Subprocessor (StorageWorks) — Redwood issues deletion + monitors completion (up to 21 days worst-case)

Attachments & evidence we can add to the packet on request: routing-table-export.txt, last-egress-test-report.pdf, supplier-deletion-clauses.pdf.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
